Author: Piger Woods
Review: I am not usually one for negative reviews because I know the struggles of running a small business but in this case I feel it is necessary. Given all the positive reviews, I was really looking forward to having a proper Sunday breakfast …MoreI am not usually one for negative reviews because I know the struggles of running a small business but in this case I feel it is necessary. Given all the positive reviews, I was really looking forward to having a proper Sunday breakfast here today. I even brought my backpack in anticipation of loading up my freezer at home. All in all, it was pretty disappointing. There were only 3 tables occupied when we got there, yet still it was around 20 minutes before our order was taken. We both ordered the Scottish breakfast because of the tattie scones and wanted additional black pudding and toast on the side. We were told there was no black pudding or even mushrooms. We were given a choice of 2 sausage types, I chose Cajun because I like a bit of spice. When the plates arrived, the tattie scone turned out to be just a triangle of fried, unseasoned, mashed potato which was mushy and very oily. No relation to a tattie scone at all. I like my eggs runny but the whites were still uncooked, very unappetising. The Cajun sausage had absolutely no flavour, not even salt, never mind spice and there was no real texture to make you feel that you were eating a quality product...just nothing. In fact the whole plate was really bland, no seasoning or flavour at all. Worse still, the sausage was raw in the middle and I left it. Surprising for a place called SausageKL. My toast didn't come so I had to ask for it and when it did arrive, it was barely warm and looked like it had been wafted over a 40 watt bulb for 5 seconds to toast it. The bacon consisted of two very small, overcooked rashers which again, had no real flavour. I can understand it if one of the items on a plate is not up to scratch but not a single element of the breakfast plate was done properly. A full cooked breakfast, when done correctly is a wonderful thing, in fact I make a pretty good one myself but when you take the time to go somewhere that specialises in this, you expect it to be good and it really, really wasn't. Our friends at the other table felt the same way. On the upside, the mug of tea was decent. They could have been having an off day today but I don't think so and I very much doubt I will go again to find out. Based on my experience today, I couldn't, in good conscience recommend SausageKL to anyone I know. I am certainly confused as to where all the positive reviews are coming from. Not good at all...My search for a decent cooked breakfast in KL continues...

First, we were given a chit for 1 hour session from 8pm to 9pm. The food took …MoreI understand that some patrons might have enjoyed this place but we were severely let down. We went impromptu based on the many positive reviews we saw on Google. First, we were given a chit for 1 hour session from 8pm to 9pm. The food took 30 mins to arrive. We ordered 3 cocktails and dinner for 3. They ran out of cakes so I ordered waffle. The shisha took more than 30 mins to prepare. In the end, we just canceled our shisha and paid for our food and drinks. 30 mins in our meal, we were asked to move tables. This was the last straw. We continued our night elsewhere. Note that the twin tower view was partial. U only get to see one tower. I think they were trying crowd control because of the mco but some poor management or communication between them resulted in delay in food and drinks. The cocktails were good and worth the money. They can probably fit 50 people max in the entire place. It's not a big place. I noted a lot of African patrons. Its such a shame that I didn't get to try their shisha which is reputed best in kl. The mixologist in bangsar did a good job. They are always spot on and reminded of my days in doha. I would probably come here for cocktails only. Trust me when I tell you that you can get better Al Faker in town.

But if you want a very nice experience or a romantic dinner I would suggest looking elsewhere as the food experience and price paid doesn't match up in my opinion :)

Author: Shaji
Review: The difference between this place and many others that I’ve been to, is attention to details, or lack thereof. …MoreThe difference between this place and many others that I’ve been to, is attention to details, or lack thereof.It was my silver jubilee, our 25th wedding anniversary. I was hosting 8 of my family members to a lunch.Throughout the lunch, not one person asked us if we were celebrating a special occasion. We’ve hosted multiple birthdays and anniversaries in the past, and almost all other restaurants we’ve hosted at have always picked up on the vibes and paid that bit more attention.While the waitress was engaging, we just couldn’t get into the mood we were expecting to.But perhaps that was because of the drinks we, my wife and I, ordered while waiting due everyone to arrive. I ordered a mojito which was bland. In fact, the Virgin mojito my wife ordered was so much better! So we stuck  to those and beers the rest of the afternoon.The food too was just mediocre. The prawns were not fresh and the dishes that contained them (most of them) expressed as much. One dish in particular was most disappointing- the squid ink pasta in a laksa fusion. The laksa sauce soaked up most of the squid ink and the prawns were just too squishy and soaked in laksa. I had expected to taste the squid ink more than the laksa but you know what they say, you won’t be disappointed if you don’t expect perfection.Of the RM500+ I spent that afternoon, only their pizzas (we tried 3) deserved a mention  That said, my sister in law makes better pizza though.This place won’t be in our list for future events.
Location: 50, Jalan Maarof, Bangsar, Wilayah Perseketuan, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Boon Loong Leo
Review: I vividly remember the very first time we came here.. it was already late at night but they still took our order and we proceed to have a quiet yet satisfying dinner in the already empty restaurant. I was glad because both of us were …MoreI vividly remember the very first time we came here.. it was already late at night but they still took our order and we proceed to have a quiet yet satisfying dinner in the already empty restaurant. I was glad because both of us were famished at that point of time and frankly, I was lazy to search for alternatives.I made it a point to revisit this restaurant again with the whole family in tow.Brunch menu:◾Fuming Duck - essentially smoked duck breast served with sherry reduction, mash, vegetables and seared plum◾Grilled calamari with sambal belacan salsa - the salsa with local twist hit the right spot as it matched the otherwise bland calamari perfectly.◾Nachos servers generously with jalapeno, tomato salsa, pulled roast chicken with melted cheese on top, and guacamole on the side... Sure fire winner with the small kids, and they even requested for the second helping.Dinner menu:◾same Fumed duck◾Al Ajillo shrimp sauteed with garlic chilly and olive oil served with garlic toast◾Wild Seabass Vongole Valoute - seared Seabass with clam Valoute and house-made sherry caviar◾French onion soup◾House pouringBoth experiences were memorable and the kids enjoyed the food a lot. Given the high turnover rate in this busy yet expensive area of Bangsar, I hope that they can stay for long time as their food and customer service rocks!
Location: 50, Jalan Maarof, Bangsar, Wilayah Perseketuan, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Although we had ordered in advance, they stood there waiting for us to order and we had to explain that we had already ordered in advance.For food we ordered the Christmas set, which was a set consisting of appetizers, main courses, and dessert. It was horrifying to see all of them on one tray as if it was a bento. Sets with more than one main course are usually for a 'fine-dining experience' which they do claim to provide and never have I experienced fine-dining served in that manner (yes, even Japanese fine-dining, I have eaten Japanese fine-dining in other Japanese fine-dining restaurants (Nobu)).Putting aside the presentation, the waitresses seemed to be majorly struggling as the bread that was supposed to be kept separate from its dip fell into the dip when served because the waitresses failed to balance it (This happened for ALL 4 sets, makes me wonder why it was served that way, should have kept it separate, because the bread proceeded to become soggy). When putting down the tray, I got rebuked by the waitress (I'm using a really mild word here in comparison of what happened) to take away my chopsticks in Cantonese, and no, she had not informed me to take it away beforehand, that was the first time she communicated such a need; there were also other waitresses there who could have helped her. When putting down two of the trays, they proceeded to place the tray right on top of the napkins. In addition to that, we had to actually inform them 5-6 times where to place each set.We were also not informed on the sequence of which the food should be eaten in. Some cutleries were also missing from the set.For drinks, we ordered sake and Japanese green tea.The serving for the green tea was terrible to say the least. The waitress insisted on serving our green tea to the brim, which, is clearly not proper etiquette as serving tea to the brim gives an implication that you want a person to leave as soon as possible (she did so from the moment the tea was served)Part of the set was the dessert which was mochi ice cream and as my sister and I could not eat cold food, we asked whether it could be substituted for anything else. The waitress merely scoffed at us and said I don't think you can and proceeded to hurry us to make a decision whether we wanted the dessert immediately. She did not even consider going out to ask whether it was possible. On her part, I think this was extremely irresponsible.Food: 0/5Appetizer: bread was soggy as I said, fish roe was overcooked.Main courses:  The oyster was extremely slimy and was not fresh, sashimi too thickly sliced, not fresh; sushi was too big, could not fit in a mouthful; lobster was an absolute horror, I think I may see it in my nightmares... it was not fresh, part of the lobster meat had not been removed (it was the type where they took out the lobster meat and then cooked it before placing it back into its shell).Drink: 1/5The green tea was certainly not the type I'd expect in this restaurant, it tasted like those in perhaps, Sushi Zanmai? Really below expectations.The 1 point goes to the sake for tasting like a proper sake.Parking service: 0/5The valets messed up the keys and proceeded on a hunt for our car keys.

Author: Shih Yuin Chew
Review: (Translated by Google) Many years ago, my friend came down from Jinbao to celebrate my birthday with me. I took her to eat her favorite eel; at that time, I came to know this Japanese restaurant in a detached house. …More(Translated by Google) Many years ago, my friend came down from Jinbao to celebrate my birthday with me. I took her to eat her favorite eel; at that time, I came to know this Japanese restaurant in a detached house.The eel here is eaten three times—original flavor, seasoning, and soup. It's worth a try. The eel itself is grilled so that the skin is dry, the meat is soft, and the sauce is deep and not overwhelming; stir in diced green onion, mustard, and seaweed, and then add a touch of freshness; then add kelp bonito broth, the multi-layered umami immediately sweeps the taste buds Something.To be honest, the three ways of eating have their own characteristics and are all delicious. Although among the three, I slightly prefer the original way of eating, but as a person who is extremely resistant to the staple food of soup, #team擂茶 does not add soup, and the method of eating with soup makes it difficult for me to give up, or even to stop.The Kabayaki eel here has always been the most cost-effective choice in my mind in the past. Although the price is high, the portion is larger; although it is no longer the highest, it is still worth it. But looking back a few years later, maybe I changed. The Kabayaki eel here feels a bit too much sauce and a bit sweeter.As for sashimi, to be honest, quite disappointed. Regardless of the quality of the fish, the part or the skill of the knife, it feels that it is not at a level that matches the level of the restaurant. For example, the fat distribution of salmon is unsatisfactory, and many sashimi are tough but uniformly cut thick, without corresponding cutting methods, or even with ribs. I remember that I was at a loss when I was eating.But what really got a little bit irritating was the king crab + foie gras dishes ordered by my friends.The king crab claw meat is covered with a thick layer of transparent starch, and the taste is similar to a tuft of potato flour when thickening failed, and then covered with greasy sauce, the deliciousness of the king crab is really submerged without a trace; and the goose The texture and taste of the liver itself is also not reflected-in my impression, this is really a 1+1 ≈0 dish that makes the raw materials false for this life.After the meal, I couldn't help but wonder: Is Ishin a Chinese-style Japanese restaurant?(Original)多年前生日 朋友从金宝下来跟我庆生，我带她吃她喜欢吃的鳗鱼；就在那时，我认识到了这家开在独立式洋房里的日本餐厅。这里的鳗鱼三吃——原味、拌料、加汤，值得一试。鳗鱼本身烤得外皮干爽、肉质酥软，酱香深沉而不泛滥；拌入葱粒、芥末、海苔，接着增添了一抹清新；再加入昆布柴魚高汤，多层复合的鲜味立刻就将味蕾席卷一番。说实在，三种吃法各有特色，也都很好吃。虽然三者之中，我略偏好原味吃法，但作为极其抗拒汤类主食的人来说 #team擂茶不加汤，加汤吃法让我同样难以割舍，甚至欲罢不能。这里的蒲烧鳗鱼，在过去一直是我心目中性价比最高的选择，价钱虽高，但份量更大；现在虽然不再见得最高，但仍然值得。不过几年后回头，或许是我变了，这里的蒲烧鳗鱼感觉酱汁有点偏多，也略甜了一点。至于刺身，说实话，相当失望。不管是鱼的品质、部位或刀工，感觉都不是和餐厅等级匹配的水准。比如三文鱼的脂肪分布差强人意，而很多鱼生都颇韧却一律厚切、没采用相应的切法，甚至带筋。记得当时我吃得一头雾水。但真正吃得有点来气的，是朋友点的帝王蟹+鹅肝料理。帝王蟹钳肉上裹了厚厚一层的透明淀粉，口感类似于勾芡失败时的一坨薯粉，再沾满油腻的酱汁，帝王蟹的鲜美真的淹没得无影无踪；而鹅肝本身口感和味道也没有体现——在我的印象里，这真的是一道1+1 ≈0，让原料虚妄此生的料理。一顿下来，我不禁都有些纳闷：Ishin是不是已经成了一家中式的日本餐厅？

The portions are great as well.For desserts, we ordered their famous strawberry cheese mille crepe cake, very unique presentation. It came as in a crepe form instead of a cake. It was heavenful. The flavours are not too overpowering each other and it has a right balance of sweetness.The waiters were attentive and friendly as well. They always come by to fill up our water glasses.Price is reasonable. Food is great. Exceptional customer service.10/10 would come here again for special occasions.

Author: Ronald Kitagawa
Review: If you’re a scotch enthusiast visiting central Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, you’ve got to swing by The Whisky Bar. This was my best scotch experience so far (I’ve not yet been to Scotland). Their collection has more than 700 different labels and …MoreIf you’re a scotch enthusiast visiting central Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, you’ve got to swing by The Whisky Bar. This was my best scotch experience so far (I’ve not yet been to Scotland). Their collection has more than 700 different labels and is a bit larger than mine (#sarcasm). The manager, Andy, posts outstanding reviews on Instagram of his latest tastings (@pot_or_column) and I had been following him from afar. It was a pleasure meeting him and sommelier Marcus and talking scotch shop with folks so knowledgeable, yet so down-to-earth. I devised my tasting lineup through Andy’s Instagram reviews and then his and Marcus’ personal advice, which all catered to my palate. The experience was so special I returned two days later for a second round of tastings. If you are a serious (or borderline serious) scotch enthusiast, you’ll want to visit during the weekday, when it’s less crowded, so you can take time to sit at the bar, relax and enjoy the camaraderie. But make sure it’s a day Andy and/or Marcus are there (I went on a Thursday and Saturday). For the scotch nerds out there, among my tastings were: Scotch Malt Whisky Society’s Linkwood 9 (A tropical breakfast), Linkwood 19 (A Blue Lady and a Seraph’s smile), Springbank 22 (A coal bucket of marshmallows), a Single Cask Macduff 19, a Single Cask The English Whisky Co. 8, and a Bowmore 29 (1982 vintage). Overall, a wonderfully memorable experience.
Restaurant: The Whisky Bar KL 威士金酒吧
Location: 46, Changkat Bukit Bintang, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Low Dywin
Review: We recently headed over to Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara to try the menu at Nizza – the hotel’s new specialty French – Mediterranean restaurant. Nizza is a refined contemporary yet casual French Riviera-inspired restaurant, with modern …MoreWe recently headed over to Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara to try the menu at Nizza – the hotel’s new specialty French – Mediterranean restaurant. Nizza is a refined contemporary yet casual French Riviera-inspired restaurant, with modern interior architectural – with light colours playing off in its interiors and a striking blue-and-white flooring. The chic pool deck ambience outside meanwhile is reminiscent of the coastline of Cote d’Azur with modern glass parasol pool bar, comfy beach cabanas, and low modular seating.The restaurant has a show kitchen where you can watch the chefs whip up a variety of specialty items a la minute. This 135-seat restaurant features a variety of seating arrangements, and is suitable for intimate dinner for two, to communal tables for groups of four or more, depending on the occasion of course. The tables are interspersed adequately apart so you won’t hear what the other table is saying while the ambience has an emphasis on unique finishing ranging from highly-detailed art deco and ceiling mural to exotic lightings and a wine cellar with a good selection of wines.On the menu are a whole range of dishes including Duck Liver Pate, Marinated White Anchovies, Nizza’s Garden Salad, Summer Niçoise Salad, Cheese Board, Garlic & Herb Crusted Spring Lamb and White Sturgeon Caviar. Among the recommended dishes are Turkey “Salchichon”, Truffle & Mushroom Croquettes, Garlic Prawns, Bouillabaisse Cote De Opal, Charcuterie Board, Salted Baked Whole Snapper, White Sturgeon Caviar as well as the Provencal and Lamb Sausage Pissaladiere. Hand-crafted cocktails and fine wines are also available to complement the cuisine.Verdict- cafe latte 5*
Restaurant: Nizza Restaurant @ Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara
Location: Level 3, Sofitel Kuala Lumpur Damansara, No. 6, Jalan Damanlela, Bukit Damansara, Kuala Lumpur

Author: Jane P
Review: *Visit my insta @janefoodbaby for more!This post is part 1/2 of the review of Beta KL festive menu ("Taste of Beta") …More*Visit my insta @janefoodbaby for more!This post is part 1/2 of the review of Beta KL festive menu ("Taste of Beta")Last year we celebrated Christmas at Skillet 163, and really amazed by how good the food was! This year we decided to go for Beta (same chef), I can only say they always deliver the best! 💯Upon walking into Cormar Suites, Beta KL has a small door covered in forest theme decorations, maybe they incorporated the speakeasy concept? Ambience of the restaurant feels more like a bar than a restaurant, but glad that they have lights shining onto each table so we can still see the beautiful presentation of food. Distance between table (side by side) was quite narrow though, and personally felt it's difficult to have a private conversation without the other guests listening.Food:1. Winged beans - The top layer is like a pear, covered in a layer of jelly. Underneath it is the winged beans in budu sauce, good combination of sweet/savory and warm/cold food. Crispy tart shell too. Definitely my favorite snack2. Pomelo w/Ikura and calamansi - Very unique texture as there's pomelo and ikura popping in your mouth. Glad that it wasn't sour at all.3. Mud crab w/kantan - The granites were too cold and sour to my liking, it hurts my salivary glands   4. Miyagi Oysters - FRESHEST AND THICKEST oyster I've ever had in my life! This is so refreshing! 😍5. Lawas rice w/mushrooms - Texture of rice is like risotto, fried cordyceps was very crispy and added good flavor to the rice.6. Turkey - Regret for picking this as main dish as the turkey was dry, bland and chewy. Probably just how turkey is but it's not my thing. Deviled/Debal sauce was good (not spicy at all) but not enough for the amount of turkey meat there. Vege could have been presented with smaller stalk. Fried potato was crispy on the outside.7. Damak chocolate - mousse was very rich and not too sweet! Portion is perfect too 💯Overall a really, really great experience! Will share more details in my next post, together with Tour of Malaysia menu 😍Part 2/2 "Tour of Malaysia" menuFood:1. Seaweed bread w/anchovies cream - This is extremely CREATIVE! While most restaurants go with kombu or truffle butter, anchovies cream was so good! For anchovies, I guess it's either you like or hate it a lot, and it happened that I LOVE it and asked for extra, while licking the anchovies cream clean 🤣2. T'lur caviar, sago on fried seaweed - This is a light and crunchy snack. No strong flavor involved, more like a cracker.3. Prawn - A savory snack, the base is what tastes like butter cookie. Prawn paste was well-blended and creamy.4. Inverted karipap - As the chef explained, instead of having potato as karipap filings, potato was used to make the round shell instead. Not spicy at all so it's great for me 😂 Best among the three snacks.5. Duck, foie gras, pumpkin - A bit of a let down cause foie gras didnt "melt", it wasn't creamy/fatty enough. Duck was salty and the fried pumpkin overpowered the taste of the entire snack ☹️6. Barramundi fish w/Tamarind sauce + add-on lobster (MYR 99) - THIS IS GOOD!! Definitely a much better option than turkey 😅 Fish is moist and tamarind sauce was very flavorful, good blend of sourness/saltiness. Lobster was poached well too.   7. Mango sorbet w/lime snow - One additional dessert compared to Taste of Beta. Refreshing, not too sour. Good pairing with the rich chocolate mousse.Left the restaurant feeling very satisfied! PERFECTLY executed modern Malaysian courses! Will definitely return again!
Location: Unit 3 & 3A, Lot, Retail, 163 No. 10, Jalan Perak, Kuala Lumpur

Review: I was very intrigued by this restaurant - my sister told me about its modern take on Malaysian cuisine - and I absolutely enjoyed the experience. I …MoreI was very intrigued by this restaurant - my sister told me about its modern take on Malaysian cuisine - and I absolutely enjoyed the experience. First of all, the interior is beautiful: contemporary design with Malaysian touches. I especially loved the colorful batik wall. There are three set menus. I ordered the Discover menu (RM 180) which was composed of six appetizers and a choice of three mains and three desserts. I thought RM 180 (~USD 40/EUR 35) for eight courses was a steal!The food was terrific! My compliments to the chef for his efforts to elevate Malaysian cuisine to a sophisticated level. The Malaysian flavors were instantly recognizable but the often surprising combination of ingredients and textures was what made the meal such a great experience. And the presentation of each dish was superb. My favorite was the crab (three types of crab layered in an egg custard and laksa broth served in a dainty cup). I also enjoyed the ‘drama’ of the Spicy Garden (cincalok with herbs and chili). The barramundi with turmeric and fermented pineapple was another great dish. The only flaw was the roti which was too oily. That’s a pity because the duck it was served with was excellent.Service was very good: attentive and informative.If you’re looking for a different (contemporary, fine-dining) take on Malaysian cuisine, I recommend Beta KL, a truly top notch restaurant a stone’s throw from the Petronas Twin Towers.

Author: Han San Lim
Review: While many would call it Indian food with a twist or something along that line, I would call a culinary delight with clever use of Indian spices. It represented India well but not at all the Indian food we grew up to know in Malaysia. Some …MoreWhile many would call it Indian food with a twist or something along that line, I would call a culinary delight with clever use of Indian spices. It represented India well but not at all the Indian food we grew up to know in Malaysia. Some may compared Nadodi to Gaggan in Bangkok, having been to Gaggan several times, I must say I enjoyed Nadodi more. Much more. Even the food vessels that were specially made for Nadodi were a visual treat.The arrival experience was not the best as parking is a bit of a challenge but soon as we stepped in to the restaurant, we were treated to a memorable journey through south India on the tip of our tongues.We started off with cocktails and all three I had were creative, refreshing and most importantly, delicious. One of them called Rasam was particularly good. A gin-base cocktail with a meringue-like topping that is warm! So delicious.We went for the 11-course option not only was it not too much, the service was brisk that it didn’t took us 3 hours to complete the meal as It was a mid week dinner after all. Meanwhile, the courses were well paced and we didn’t feel rushed.It was a very successful 11 course and 10 out of the 11 were faultless while not so much a failure of the chef, I didn’t care for one of the 2 desserts that was flavored with cardamom. Since the menu changes every 2 months, no point going through each course here, but all of them were very good.The 11-course were only priced at RM450+/-, it was well worth the money. Mind you, the dinner was nothing sort of what you can get at top restaurants in New York, Hong Kong or London, I challenge anyone to eat this well in a restaurant at such standard and pay less than US$120 for it.
Location: Lot 183, 1st Floor Jalan Mayang, Off, Jalan Yap Kwan Seng, Kampung Baru, Kuala Lumpur

Review: Had the 11-mile journey on 14th July: Interesting fine dining experience and food inspired by the tastes of India, Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka, etc. Its food packs a punch of flavour with one or two being too overpowering (chicken noodle soup) …MoreHad the 11-mile journey on 14th July: Interesting fine dining experience and food inspired by the tastes of India, Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka, etc. Its food packs a punch of flavour with one or two being too overpowering (chicken noodle soup) and underwhelming (lobster muesli). Service is good, as expected for restaurants at this price point. The main reasons for the 3 stars are: Parking: The limited parking at The Mayang Place is reserved for guests of the Mayang Club. Fine. I was directed to the back of the building where the jockey for the restaurant is. Jockey is RM15, but the guy couldn't speak any English on where the car will be parked despite me asking in very simple english. I had my concerns as I wouldn't want my car to be left on the roadside seeing how limited the parking there is. So I decided to park at the Bangunan Getah behind, which is RM4 per entry after hours and walked 2 minutes to the restaurant. Secondly, the 9 and 11-mile journey serves different food and my family would like to experience all by mixing up the orders. However, upon deciding, we were told by the waiter that they only serve one type of "journey" per table. I.e. everyone has to order the same thing, as they claimed that the kitchen would mess up the orders and timing of the dishes will be awkward. To us it's fine if the intention of the restaurant is for the guests to have the same experience throughout...but please pre-inform when laying out the menu, and don't give excuses such as "the kitchen will be confused". Seriously...Anyways, pro-tip:1. Take a cab/ ride-hailing car there2. Be prepared to order the same thing for the whole table.3. Corkage is RM150, but get the first bottle waived.4. Try this once, but to me, not worth a second visit at this price.

Author: Gifford
Review: Fantastic and unique experience! Have always wanted to give this dining experience a try, why not? Made my booking online with some discount. …MoreFantastic and unique experience! Have always wanted to give this dining experience a try, why not? Made my booking online with some discount.As you head up to the restaurant, already you get the feel of what's to come, low lighting and calm ambience awaits you and your partner. You will be seated in front of the bar as they prepare you for dinner, they served a virgin aperitif and asked us to guess the ingredients. Next was a blindfold game and then it was time to go in for dinner. Handphones and watches will be kept in a locker, basically anything that reflects or produced light, stored my glasses as well since I'll have no use for it😂Our servers were visually impaired and would lead us to our table, I thought this was brilliant and proud to support this establishment who employed such servers, if you think about it, who better to guide you than those who live everyday in darkness.I would recommend to dine as a couple because this experience forces you to a different level of intimacy and communication, there were groups and other partners during my experience. There was 1 table with a cantonese speaking aunty which made me feel like I was in a kopitiam.4 course meal with each meal being a mystery. As you are served each dish, your server will explain and suggest the best way to consume your dish. This is where the fun begins and you have to teach yourself to eat again. The room is completely pitch black and you can't even see your ✋ in front of your face.Guys, if you're coming because of the food and easily irritated for not knowing what you're eating then don't waste your time here. The food actually is delicious but I know some people can't stand or are picky about what they're going to eat. Have heard of an experience where someone was very frustrated spending so much and unable to see if you've finish everything on your plate.Completely enjoyed my time and meal experience, felt like a kid try new foods again. The restaurant changes menu every 3 months and everything was pleasant and exciting for the first time. Definitely will come back to see if the experience could be replicated.

Just try to not have expectations and you will surely be happy you went.More on the food: we had the vegan menu. I appreciated so much that DitD KL had an understanding of veganism and had readily available vegan options. And they are improving all the time, I imagine.Appetizers were the best. True five stars! Soups were solid, mains were good. The deserts we not imaginative, unfortunately. We were really looking forward to them, but were a bit disappointed: cut up bananas, canned lychee were used to replace the cheesecake and the brownie respectively (from the regular menu). Hey, at least we can be sure it’s all vegan!Still, we thought the food was great overall. The chefs are doing their best to accommodate vegans and we really appreciated that effort here. I guess it goes along the lines of the general energy of this place: we are all equal and we all deserve respect and a possibility to exist comfortably and happily. Glad to support this.Service: top notch, with a touch of family warmth. Perfect from start to finish.Ambiance: lovely venue (coincides with a jazz bar), great soft instrumental music playing in the dark room, spacious veranda to relax on and digest the experience.Bottom line: ideal for dark first timers! The staff couldn’t be nicer and you will feel well taken care of. Come out and support equality for all people.

Author: G U Renukanand
Review: Probably the best Italian restaurant in Damansara. I have heard so much about this place and finally got a chance to bring my family there. …MoreProbably the best Italian restaurant in Damansara. I have heard so much about this place and finally got a chance to bring my family there.A great selection of Italian food and pasta which is made at the restaurant. So you are not getting any cold frozen pasta reheated and served in a platter.Kicked off the evening with. zucchini parmagiana , typically you would get a eggplant but here they have replaced it with zucchini. Both vegetables add such an unique experience to the dish. I was expecting a baked dish but this was served in three portions and topped with freshly grated cheese.Next up was the Burrata on a plate of cherry tomatoes tossed in olive oil,  balsamic vinegar and fresh greens. The fresh creamy Burrata and the sweet cheery 🍅 were a treat in the mouth.Who doesn't love a good 🍕. This was our main course for the night. Started off with a four cheese pizza and then ended up ordering another Margarita pizza. At this point the chef came to our table and explained how each dish is specially made. He was quick to point out that there is less than 2% yeast in the dough and they allow the dough to raise over a 3 day period.I have to say it was one of the best pizza dough we have had in Kuala Lumpur. Crusty on the outside with a pillows of air bubbles all over.The chef didn't want us to leave with having tried his pasta and we were treated with a small portion of Ricotta cheese and spinach tortellini with a butter sauce. We were licking the sauce out of our fingers. It was just incredible.The Italian chef is an avid travelled with experiences from all over the world.A dinner for 2 could easily be in the range of RM 150-200 with wine and with desserts it can be upto RM 250.If you are seated outside and the weather is pleasant it's a treat. Do call for reservations as they are usually packed for dinners. Most patrons enjoy the meal and are not rushed to finish the meal for the next customer.Great service and attention by the team at Nero Nero.On not to forget the Lemoncello which was served to us in the end 😘
Location: L3 - 02, Jalan Damanlela, Damansara City Mall, Damansara Town Centre, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur

Review: The food they serve is not just delicious but with good portions too. They have trainee servers from the orang asli community and refugees. They have trainee servers from the orang asli community and refugees. Eat X doubles up as a training ground for them under this social enterprise by Dignity for Children Foundation. Eat X is a good example of food which is of high quality, but doesn't necessarily have to cost a bomb. Prices range from RM12 for the huge bowl of Nyonya Laksa (totally recommended), RM18 for a beautifully spread out Nasi Kerabu with Ayam Percik (using ingredients from their Grow X garden), Nasi Ulam for vegetarians at RM18, beef burger and other delectable dishes (google their menu). Oh, don't forget to try their Salted Egg Croissant and Green Thai Pasta. While there, get your haircut at Cut X and tailored items at Sew X (lovely face masks). They are all within the vicinity of Sentul Boulevard. The only downside is that to get empty parking spots is quite a challenge. If you're coming at peak hours and in groups, pls call ahead. With the new SOP (Covid 19), they have to distance the spacing a bit. Worth coming back many times to sample all their offerings. Have tea/coffee and their home made cakes too (baked at Bake X)! Bring friends and family to impress! They would also come back for more!!

The dim sum buffet is very reasonably priced at under RM30 pp (I think it was RM28 or RM29). But quality and taste is under par. The duck and wantan noodles were alright though. We were told that we were not allowed to do this. I can understand and support avoiding wastage. But I wanted to pack up my leftovers to finish up at home. Is that so bad? There were also no notices or warnings to say that customers were not allowed to take away leftovers. So I felt like we were trapped into paying the surcharge for our leftovers. That was not a pleasant experience.

It was resolved automatically as we moved to Phase 4 and the restrictions eased a bit.The ambiance was great. Very hygienic.Very friendly staff and they keep you engaged.The food was presented flawlessly and was a  feast to the eyes. The experience itself is excellent and keeps you so involved throughout the 90 minutes.On the con side, the time limit between one course and the next should be a bit more longer and not hurry us up in finishing the course.Not all courses were great. The Indian menu felt like we tasted some granules of sand (It could be roasted spices that popped in the mouth), but probably the Chef should re-consider serving this dish on the menu.All the other dishes were commendable , not to forget the lemon sorbet. It was overall a great and memorable experience to be etched in our memories minus the couple of cons.The dessert was excellent and presented brilliantly. Thank you Le Petit chef!Also, I had already mentioned at the time of the booking that it was our anniversary celebrations, so as an extra mile, I would have been thrilled, if you could have offered a small cake/dessert to celebrate the same, would have been more thoughtful and  would have made it a great experience for me on a personal note.

The 3 stars in my review is just for that.The bad - Michelin star or not, the food was absolutely totally ordinary. I suppose the menu is rather limited given that the videos do to a certain extent dictate the menu. But there are plenty of chefs in KL (with zero Michelin stars) that could have done better. Flavours were flat and the produce was not fresh (especially the seafood). Worst of all, the portions are tiny. So expect to leave hungry. The manager actually had the nerve to explain that "oh Michelin star dishes are supposed to be small". Give me a break and save that excuse for the backwater rednecks that don't know any better.The ugly - the dinner has to start for everyone simultaneously. As such, if the majority of people arrive late, then they cannot start. I was sadly one of the few that did come on time (early actually, as instructed by their booking confirmation) and yet the proprietor did NOTHING to start on time. I waited almost 1 and a half hours for my dinner to begin. So don't tell people to come early if you're not going to start on time!!

Author: Nash Johari
Review: That instinct to search for a ‘lepak and makan’ makes Kuala Lumpur an especially fun place to live and eat - the city’s charming urban fabric are famous for hiding all manner of culinary riches. …MoreThat instinct to search for a ‘lepak and makan’ makes Kuala Lumpur an especially fun place to live and eat - the city’s charming urban fabric are famous for hiding all manner of culinary riches.One such ‘makan place’, the Malai Thai Cuisine at the Fraser Place KL, had its potential for charm. Located neatly in the middle of the golden triangle KL, it’s a walking distance from our office as well as all the main attraction around from KL Tower to KLCC to Bukit Bintang. If you driving there, they have valet service at your disposal.Malai is Thai name for a flower garland that you will almost certainly see everywhere in Thailand. It’s a symbol for luck and respect. We were told the restaurant is barely few weeks old, yet the staff is polite and attentive to our food order, which is part of what makes Malai so delightful.Having heard the head chef is a native Thai’s who combined traditional thai with a twist of modern flavor, we decided to try few combinations and shared across the table. We start with a spring rolls, followed by Gaeng keawwaan Thai green curry, deep-fried shrimp with tamarind sauce and stir-fry mix vegetable to name a few. The service is quick, the food served with fresh ingredients with great flavours, intensely aromatic, and kind of mesmerizing when paired with spicy Prawn Tum Yum.We finished the lunch with sticky rice drown in fresh coconut milk, and sweet Thai mangoes on the side. It was a lovely combination of flavours and we thoroughly enjoyed it. Can't fault this. Simple, and wonderful.. Presentation on point, taste is beyond expectation.
Location: Cormar Suites, 10, Jalan Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Ralph Yong
Review: Manja consist of a two-storey space with corners galore to explore which including an amazing glass-ceiling lounge upstairs where customers bask beneath the lights of the KL Tower. All in all, a destination to remember. …MoreManja consist of a two-storey space with corners galore to explore which including an amazing glass-ceiling lounge upstairs where customers bask beneath the lights of the KL Tower. All in all, a destination to remember.Manja has a unique menu that ensemble original dishes that different from other borders & boundaries which layering familiar Malaysian flavours & textures from influences across the globe. There's combination of sushi joints from Japan to the tapas bars of Spain, the soul food shops of New Orleans to the osterias of Tuscany. Let's start with small plates for sharing, Borneo Coconut Tuna which cost RM48. The ingredients includes morsels of line-caught tuna sashimi with extra virgin coconut oil, organic coconut milk, roasted dessicated coconut, cashews, red rubin basil & chives, with a side of tapioca chips.For my friend who love beef, his choice would be Wagyu Gula Melaka that priced at RM188. Meat tableau of tenderness, from the first bite to the final chew. Weight at 200 grammes of smooth prime beef filled into a powerhouse of flavour with a boost from palm sugar, unconventionally but irresistibly complemented with velvety Japanese rice, egg, & sauteed shimeji & shiitake mushrooms for a no-holds-barred platter of protein & carbs worth loosening the belt for. A recommended antidote to quell steak cravings.

It was a little too much on the rare side, which makes it just a little bit chewy, but absolutely great flavors as well, the garlic-fried rice is just a little too big a portion, but delicious. Review: The food was very good and I would revisit. But I have to agree with others comments that they are a bit pushy on getting you to order more than you need. Upon hearing that we will not be ordering drinks, they seem a bit disappointed. When …MoreThe food was very good and I would revisit. But I have to agree with others comments that they are a bit pushy on getting you to order more than you need. Upon hearing that we will not be ordering drinks, they seem a bit disappointed. When two of us (female petite) decided we will only order 2 medium dishes, I could almost see her eyes drop out from rolling too hard. She said “just this, no drinks not even appetizer?” Yep I said - thanks to the reviews I knew we may not finish the food if we had ordered more. True enough, we couldn’t even finish just that two dishes. I’m surprised even after so many reviews commenting that us customers hate to be pushed to order more - it’s not recommendation it was pushy. They are still doing it and not afraid that people will not revisit. Anyway, the food was nice, I would revisit to try others on the menu and the cocktails that they claimed was very popular. However I will not let them decide how much I want to order. Order what you need, if it’s not enough then add more. Don’t be pressured and don’t let them ruin your night out :)Ps- when the review is so much more focused on pushing customers to order more, you know sth is wrong - even if the food is good - you need to look into it and stop doing it. Maybe stop being in denial :)

Review: Best Promises Are The One’s Which We KeepFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-in …MoreBest Promises Are The One’s Which We KeepFirst off, this is a review on their food delivery and not dine-inService: We placed the order via Whatsapp and was greeted by a polite & informative customer service who made pretty good recommendations.Packaging: From a by-stander’s point of view, not knowing what was within, it looks more like a beautifully wrapped gift set emitting an extremely seductive scent of truffleSpring Signature (RM 198)1 x Dried Longan Bread Loaf1 x Truffles Butter (100g)1 x Kulim Butter (80g)1 x Soup of the Day1 x Mushroom & Summer Truffles Penne1 x Saute Vegetables2 x Pomme Puree with Homemade Duck Bacon1 x Pumpkin Puree2 x Slow Cooked Duck Leg1 x Torched Baby CabbageTaste: The promise of providing a no-frills personalised dining experience at an affordable price, seems ambitious but Skillet has begged to differ. The thought of the juiciness of the duck finished off with a touch of cranberry makes us hungry all over again. The penne was al dente with a sprinkle of freshly shaved truffle accompanied by a rich & creamy mushroom sauce. The texture of the soup of the day was creamy & had a rich flavour of broccoli delighting the diner with each spoonful.We concluded the meal with a customized Cempedak tart fulfilling their promise of a personalized dining experience.Price: Reasonable for the quality & variety of foodRecommended? Though some may say they were trying to hard, we think they were simply delivering their mouth watering promise in the form of a gift box set to lift one’s spiritsOur full review is on Instagram (@monk3yseendo)

Enam and Azim are great!But then the food. Let me tell you from a local perspective. It’s sucks. For its price. It’s sucks. We ordered the crab. 18rm per gram. We chose the big one, 850gm that’s 153rm for a Beautiful mud crab. WASTED. The chef, he pan fried it with oil till it was dry and devoid of moisture. Crabs are over 80% water and this big crab’s flesh was reduced to a wrinkled dry and tiny mess. When the crab was cracked open, the remaining dehydrated dry flesh was just a tiny slither inside a big claw shell. The frying also caused a lot of the dry flesh to stick onto the inner walls of the shells thus leaving more content for the rubbish bin more than our stomachs. We live in Malaysia and Malaysia is king of crab dishes. Chinese restaurants serve crabs everywhere and the basic knowledge is not known to a fine dining chef. Ruined. Crab ruined.Then the lamb. It’s sucks too. Medium well. But just not great. Rubber texture and no crispy fats and charred surface. No juicy tender meat. Heat was not enough. Rack of lamb is a bbq grilled dish. Not a stew. I’m a grilled lamb specialist foodie. So maybe my standards are high. I expect crispy hot fats over charred surface meat with juicy sealed juices on the inside tender meat.Consolidation, staff was great. Amazing staff. And butter garlic scallop was good. 3 big pieces for 28rm. Can la....expensive but fine dining right? Can accept. But the crab and the lamb. Shows how much they know about the art of cooking. Chef fail. Never coming back again. I don’t recommended Malaysians to eat there. Maybe for one time tourists who never coming back again anyways. Malaysian locals will find this standard very low in terms of cooking method and dining taste texture and experience.Side note, thank you Enam for the cake at the end. Super appreciate that. You are awesome.

On the day we went to the restaurant and told them we have …MoreI really regret bringing my gf for her birthday dinner over here. I made reservation through tableapp with some notes for them to provide a small piece of cake for my gf birthday. On the day we went to the restaurant and told them we have made reservation. The waiter check their booking list and yes my name was there. But, none of them was aware of what I've stated on my reservation. I didn't make an issue/complain since I didn't wanted to spoil our dinner date. The person in charge added that their kitchen will be open at 6pm sharp and we was told only live cooking available which was happening infront of the restaurant. We was there around 5pm and fine since I was aware that dinner they serve from 6pm onwards. We just ordered few dish on their live cook menu. Since, they was not aware what I wanted from my booking. I explained to the person in charge regarding my gf birthday and asked him whether he can provide a small piece of cake. He said sure. So, we were waiting for the kitchen to be open while having dish we ordered from the live cooking. Once the watch hit 6pm, I called the waiter to order and he said need to wait 10mins since all the chef is outside on the live cooking event I said okay since just 10mins. After another 15mins, I called another waiter to ask whether I can place my order and he said it will take another 10mins. Both of us decided to not order anything. Then, we told the waiter we don't want to order anything else just bring the cake. He said okay and walk off. Another 10-15 mins, no one show up. I got pissed off. I went to the one who said will bring the cake `shortly' and requested for bill. Also I told him to cancel the cake. But he said sry sir. I'll bring it now. I mean this how you treat your customer? If you can't open your kitchen sharp 6pm. Pls don't promise to your customers. So they won't be waiting or they might find some other alternatives. But the cake part is totally unacceptable, its not like you're baking a new fresh piece of cake. I wonder why it took almost 15mins. Cake was serve within the mention duration since I complained. Or else it might have taken even more time.Please teach your waiter what is the definition of 'surprise'. Your waiter just came and saying infront of my gf I'll give complementary cake since we overlooked your booking. Wth, I request cake for my gf birthday not as complementary item. My gf surprise birthday celebration was really a disaster. This is the first and last going to this restaurant.

Author: EuGene Liew
Review: This steakhouse is among the better steakhouses in Kuala Lumpur. It is located next to The Whiskey Bar along the Changkat street. Upon entering, the interior of this restaurant speaks of old-American steakhouse with brick walls and dimly …MoreThis steakhouse is among the better steakhouses in Kuala Lumpur. It is located next to The Whiskey Bar along the Changkat street. Upon entering, the interior of this restaurant speaks of old-American steakhouse with brick walls and dimly lit interior.We started off the meal with some complimentary bread and butter. The bread was warm and butter freshly made. We were also served mushroom soup compliments from the chef. It had good consistency and bits of mushrooms within. Next were the Crab Cakes and Beef Capparcio. The Crab Cakes has a good amount of crab meat inside and cooked just right while maintaining the moisture. Beef Capparcio was thinly sliced and did not break easily. The seasoning was on point and had a good amount of Parmesan cheese shavings. The serving was enough for 2-3 adults.Next we had the main course including a Tenderloin steak (200g), Striploin (300g) and BBQ Short Ribs. The Tenderloin was served Medium Rare but it was slightly too dry for our liking. The seasoning was on point. The sides of Battered Onion Rings felt unnecessary. It was too hard and not crunchy. Seasoned vegetables were used as the base for the steak and had a good bite to them. They were well seasoned and not overly cooked. As for the potato side, do go for their Garlic Mash. The Baked Potato was undercooked and dry. The Striploin steak was much better given the amount of fat with the cut. It was juicy and well seasoned. All the steaks came with a side of Salsa as well which had a good flavour and sharpness to it. They also served the steaks with 5 different kinds of salts which helped elevate the flavour of the steak. A nice touch that helped make this place standout. Though I would have preferred if they served some mustard with the steak. The sauces were quite redundant as the steaks tasted much better without them. But if you had to choose a sauce, go for the Red Wine. Lastly, the BBQ Short Ribs were soft and moist with the meat falling off the bone with ease.The meal ended with a Crepe Suzette which was prepared tableside. It tasted okay and slightly too sweet for our liking.Overall, this place is on par with steakhouses like Beato and Ril’s in term of price point and quality of steaks. If you are looking for a steak joint within downtown KL city, do give this place a try!
Restaurant: The Steakhouse KL 章卡牛排之馆
Location: 48, Changkat Bukit Bintang, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Accompanied with bread and butter, i would have been very comfortable just with this if the portion was big enough.The 4 of us enjoyed two grilled prawns that came with a awesome gravy, a very good aglio and superb lamb cutlets. For dessert we had the panacotta and the crepe suzette, both of which was very good.For whisky, a 21y Glen Keith by a Malaysian independent bottler, Eiling Lim. I enjoyed it neat but towards the end i added a touch of water and boy was i blown away. It was almost a different experience. And certainly well worth the price. Kudos to Eiling wherever you are.

At the end of Kuala Lumpur's "Party Mile" is the nicely furnished restaurant with an attached whiskey lounge. The service is attentive and friendly from the start. The menu has a good selection of steak dishes. You can choose side dishes and sauces yourself, you get a selection of homemade flavored salts and a variation of 3 homemade mustard varieties. The steak was fried to the point. The sauces tasted very fine and the side dishes were fresh and perfectly cooked. You can also find seafood and other dishes on the menu. A large selection of tempting desserts, including a Belgian chocolate fountain, also makes the hearts of those with a sweet tooth beat faster. Our crêpes Suzette, tasted wonderful, was flambéed fresh at the table. Where can you get that today? The wine list is great, French classics, well-known Italian names, Spain's top winemakers but also wines from Agentinia, Chile, NZ and many more can be found. It's worth taking a look at the wine cellar. As a finale, we treated ourselves to fine wiskys from the Wisky Bar, which in itself is a highlight. The prices are absolutely ok and we had a great evening.(Original)Das Restaurant hat uns aufgrund der Bewertungen angesprochen. Am Ende der "Party Meile" von Kuala Lumpur befindet sich das schön eingerichtete Restaurant mit angegliederter Whisky Lounge. Der Service ist vom Anfang an aufmerksam und freundlich. In der Speisekarte findet sich eine gute Auswahl an Steakgerichten. Man kann Beilagen und Saucen selber wählen, erhält eine Auswahl an hausgemachten aromatisierten Salzen sowie eine Variation von 3 hausgemachten Senfsorten. Das Steak war auf den Punkt gebraten. Die Saucen sehr fein abgeschmeckt und die Beilagen frisch und perfekt gegarrt. Man findet aber auch Seafood und andere Gerichte auf der Karte. Eine große Auswahl an verführerischen Dessert unter anderem einen belgischen Schokoladenbrunnen, lässt auch die Herzen von Naschkatzen höher schlagen. Unser Crêpes Suzette, hat wunderbar geschmeckt, wurde frisch am Tisch flambiert. Wo bekommt man das heute noch? Die Weinkarte ist großartig, französische Klassiker, italienische bekannte Namen, SpaniensTop Winzer aber auch Weine aus Agentinien, Chile, NZ und viele mehr sind zu finden. Ein Blick in den Weinkeller lohnt sich. Als Finale haben wir uns noch feine Wiskys aus der Wisky Bar gegönnt, was allein für sich schon ein Highlight ist. Die Preise sind absolut ok und wir hatten einen tollen Abend.

Author: Jin
Review: In Asia, Sunday brunch buffet at a hotel restaurant is an institution.  There is no shortage of choice of foods, themes, vibe, and price.  Curate at the Four Season in KL is at the more glitzy end of the Sunday brunch buffet and it …MoreIn Asia, Sunday brunch buffet at a hotel restaurant is an institution.  There is no shortage of choice of foods, themes, vibe, and price.  Curate at the Four Season in KL is at the more glitzy end of the Sunday brunch buffet and it certainly shows with the impeccable service and quality of foods.  Where it fails (for me) is the seemingly confused variety of foods on offer.  There is certainly an international selection of foods but it felt thrown together and just didn’t come together.  That said, if it was a dish that strikes your fancy, it was generally well made and tasty.  I can’t put my finger on it but something was missing and as a result there weren’t many memorable dishes but I still ate it all.  One section that didn’t disappoint was the desserts and that was to me the showcase of the buffet.  A solid blend of east and west, it ended my Sunday gluttony in just the right way and I left satisfied.  Give it a go and see if you feel the same.
Location: 145, Jln Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Review: I've never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has offered better service and hospitality than Curate, Four Seasons. I went to the restaurant to celebrate my mother's birthday and I was not disappointed. …MoreI've never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has offered better service and hospitality than Curate, Four Seasons. I went to the restaurant to celebrate my mother's birthday and I was not disappointed.The atmosphere is what you can expect out of a five star hotel. Curate will make you feel like you're in the shoes of a millionaire for a day. Marble floors, art decors that span a dining table for twelve, and warm tones reflected off the lighting. There's that perfect amount of space to explore what the restaurant has to offer without feeling like you're going to bump into someone's table. It's luxurious but you don't feel ostracized or out of place.At the time, the buffet was split into a small selection of regional dishes. Local, Middle Eastern, and Italian. There's dessert, a cheese platter, a salad bar and a selection of juices. That was it. However, all of them were immaculately presented and they tasted amazing. The texture of the beef rendang, the hummus, the lamb, was on point. There was nothing up for offer that wasn't a burst of flavors. Quality over quantity. Every meal was fresh to the taste and warm to the touch.The service was the main feature to write home about. The waiters and waitresses were always attentive. They made sure that our plates were replaced once we were done eating and that our glasses were never empty. While I was browsing through the buffet, Chef Qal introduced himself to me and asked me how the food was. He was heartwarmingly friendly and we got along well. He told me the process the Curate staff goes through to ensure the food's freshness and how the restaurant determines what dishes they would like to put on display. It was an insightful experience made even better when he arbitrarily planned out a celebration the moment he heard that I was here to celebrate my mother's birthday. On the house, Chef Qal ensured that their customers were having the best experience was the restaurant's top priority.I say it again because I cannot stress it enough. I have never been to a restaurant in Malaysia that has given me and my family this amount of love, friendliness and hospitality. I recommend this restaurant to everyone.
Location: 145, Jln Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Saiful Jazri Zahari
Review: I was sceptical at first when I read all the reviews in here saying that this Italian restaurant is one of the best in town. Many claim to be the best but fall so far behind it. …MoreI was sceptical at first when I read all the reviews in here saying that this Italian restaurant is one of the best in town. Many claim to be the best but fall so far behind it.Took the chance and booked this restaurant for my better half's birthday lunch. Didn't want to set any expectations because the last Italian restaurant I went to was a let down.Service was prompt and friendly. Took a starter, soup, pasta and pizza. The 4 must haves to properly give the restaurant a holistic review. Since it's just going to be just the 2 of us divulging, we decided the dishes to be for sharing. For starters we had deep fried calamari and then took the wild mushroom soup with truffles. Pasta was recommended by the server. It was the carbonara pasta and for pizza we had the classic cheese with spicy beef salami.After finishing the complimentary bread which was just amazing with the standard olive oil and  vinegar dip, came the soup. A waft of the truffle oil is enough to whet your appetite. The mushroom soup was heavenly. The cream, the taste of wild mushrooms and truffle oil compliment each other tastefully and neither overpowered each other.Then came white deep fried calamari. We were surprised to see the generous portion. The batter was almost tempura light but the squid were super very fresh and soft. I haven't seen calamari as white as those as if the chef went down to the docks and picked them out himself.Next came the signature carbonara e  castlemagno spaghetti. The spaghetti mixes with cream, egg yolk and beef bacon and later mixed in a bowl of aged Castlemagno cheese wheel brought in from Italy and flamed on the inside beforehand to soften some of the cheese from the huge block. They then mix in the spaghetti with cream and scrape the inside of the cheese block to give you this sticky cheesy carbonara spaghetti. No added salt was put in. I did find it lacking in salt but the cheese made it up in flavorfull undertones and creamy rich texture. A must try.Last but not least, what would an Italian restaurant be without its pizza. 2 pages of pizza on the menu. One page classic Italian and the other page chef's recipe. We took the classic tomato based cheese with spicy beef salami and guess what? One of the best I've had. The tomato base sauce and the cheese made the perfect pair on this bed of sourdough  that had scattering of thinly sliced spicy beef salami. Now this pizza was awesome.All in all, we had an excellent time at Prego. 5 star service with 6 star rated food.
Location: Level G, 199, Jln Bukit Bintang, Bukit Bintang, Kuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur

I still requested for their tomato sauce. Crusty in the outside while warm and soft on the inside.. i would have finished it if not saving space for other dishes.◾ Pizza Quattro Formaggi - this was something the 3 kids could agree on for dinner. And one pizza could easily feed them all.◾ Insalata Caprese - buffalo mozzarella, heirloom tomato, basil and pine nut emulsion, fresh basil and finally drizzled with extra virgin olive oil. Love the presentation and all the combinations worked well together◾ Cozze alla Tarantina - black mussels with arrabiata sauce and focaccia bread on the side. Nothing beats fresh mussels although the sauce could be better◾ Salt-crusted sea bass, steamed new potatoes, fennel, and lemon butter sauce - this was probably the longest dish to prepare, taking about 30 minutes. The waiter was show you the whole fish before filleting it right in front of you. Please squeeze the lemon on the fish and request for black pepper as it was bland as the lemon butter sauce could not work wonder itself.◾ Dinner was completed with a bottle of Gran VinaSol, a white wine from Spain which was fitting as we were having seafood.Speaking of which, I still love coming to Prego although the standard is not the same as the first time I came many years ago. Besides great coffee (which I can get at Kopitiam for cheaper) and ice cream (I can buy from supermarket) the food was passable but the presentation needs improvement. When food critics come they get full attention to being served well and with the best presentation & preparation of the dishes being touted. And they are seated in the elegant downstairs. I expected the higher ups in the kitchen would accept responsibility without passing the buck down to the lowest level staff. Putting the onus on lowest common denominator to ensure quality of service, food & preparation makes me very reluctant to give honest feedback. I rather just pay and never return. So if manager levels come apologise, which is appreciated, please get everyone to up the team's game with feedback & training rather than push responsibility downwards. Author: Ralph Yong
Review: Four Seasons features a collection of romantic menus throughout Curate, Pool Bar & Grill, The Lounge, and Decadent this Valentine’s Day. These restaurants offer the best experiences for couples looking for a romantic dining experience to …MoreFour Seasons features a collection of romantic menus throughout Curate, Pool Bar & Grill, The Lounge, and Decadent this Valentine’s Day. These restaurants offer the best experiences for couples looking for a romantic dining experience to celebrate birthdays, anniversaries, and any other special occasions.At Four Seasons Kuala Lumpur, romantic experiences and custom menus that are specially tailored to your preferences are available all day, not just on Valentine’s Day.Their philosophy: “Treat others the way you would want to be treated” is promising and so is their reputation. In the end, it comes to the time, when we forget about statements and just enjoy the Four Seasons Kuala Lumpur high tea.On to the afternoon tea service. The choice of tea would be the Lounge’s Tropical Signature Blend, described as a blend of black & green teas, enhanced by tropical flavours of hibiscus, guava, coconut, strawberry, marigold & cornflowers.The comestibles came in a 3-tiered serving tray contraption. The sandwich was described as Chicken Carnation on their menu. On top of the middle glass tray, got four pieces of savory high tea party food. The most color-popping addition was a red tea sandwich filled with salmon and X.O sauce. The red colored bread could also serve as a warning for the notable chili addition. Next to the chili, could also taste the cured radish, fresh cucumber, and parsley.

Author: Saiful Jazri Zahari
Review: The Lounge at Four Seasons is a place to go for hi tea and to have a quiet luncheon with friends, family or clients. Slightly informal setting, you get to choose from a semi circle lounge chairs to low sofa and tables and a unique 7 seater …MoreThe Lounge at Four Seasons is a place to go for hi tea and to have a quiet luncheon with friends, family or clients. Slightly informal setting, you get to choose from a semi circle lounge chairs to low sofa and tables and a unique 7 seater table cut from a huge piece of marble.Service was excellent. Prompt, professional, helpful and friendly. The Nasi Lemak Surf and Turf was unique. Comes with beef rib rendang and half lobster cooked in sambal. The dish  wasn't hot but well marinated and seasoned with spices. A good complex taste from the succulent beef rib rendang and tender meat from half a lobster cooked in sambal. The sambal coated the lobster meat well.The wagyu beef burger was also amazing. Cooked medium rare or to your liking, the marbelling or fat intertwined in the beef to make the burger moist enough but a layer of sauteed onions and mushrooms helped out with the taste. Portion was sizeable for one or if you're a small eater, share it with another.To get the most of the burger, you need to cut a slice of the burger with the bun and onions and mushroom, eat it while slicing a small piece of pickle and combining it with the burger and the taste comes together. The fatty Wagyu beef, the sauteed onions, the mushrooms and the pickle perfectly compliments each other.For dessert, if you love strawberry cheesecake, then this is the one for you. The best strawberry cheesecake I've tasted so far. The base is crunchy and tasty, the cheese wasn't too sweet and the imported fresh strawberries was juicy and sweet. Still salivating while I'm typing this.Truly an amazing experience at The Lounge with the live piano (apologies because I thought it was from a CD) as it was very good. Overall experience, loved it. Will definitely come back again.
Location: 145, Jln Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: Elvi Thio
Review: Hands down, the best omakase restaurant in KL which I wasn't expecting AT ALL. I mean, no one really talks about this place and it doesn't really show up in those "best omakse spots in KL" lists, so I thought it'd be like any other spot but …MoreHands down, the best omakase restaurant in KL which I wasn't expecting AT ALL. I mean, no one really talks about this place and it doesn't really show up in those "best omakse spots in KL" lists, so I thought it'd be like any other spot but nooo, this place is bomb. I just don't think they do any marketing and their restaurant is so small and hidden (behind an oyster bar in the basement of the Four Seasons hotel), it's unassuming.I gotta admit, probably one of the pricier omakase spots? But you don't always get premium food at premium prices, and at Hibiki you DEFINITELY do. I opted for the RM750 per person omakase (Miyabi course). The less expensive is RM520 for non-premium ingredients and the more expensive is RM980 if you want to customize it and work with the chef on something Idk special.They put a lot of love, effort, and thought into everything they serve here, you can taste it in every bite. You can also tell by the way the staff (chefs + waiters) are so excited to share information about the ingredients and their process of preparing everything. They have a book handy so they can always show you exactly what you are eating! They get shipments from Japan 2-3 times a week and everything comes FRESH, NOT FROZEN!! You can taste it in their ikura (salmon roe eggs), the saltiness is so mild and it's because they get the fish fresh and dig out the eggs themselvessss. I think this was the best ikura I've ever had. I'm sure 95% of most sushi restaurants get that stuff shipped in frozen lol.I loved everything they had, which was a mix of hot + cold dishes, but the highlights were that ikura, monkfish liver, their super comforting hot red miso soup, and of course the sushi all delicious fresh and some perfect bursts of flavors in your mouth.
Location: Lot B1-04(A), Basement 1 Shoppes at Four Seasons Place KL, 145, Jln Ampang, Kuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur

Author: Micheal Wallace
Review: A true Japanese sushi bar dining experienceSushi Hibiki is one of the best sushi bars that I've ever visited in Kuala Lumpur. They serve the finest-quality, in-season ingredients imported from across the …MoreA true Japanese sushi bar dining experienceSushi Hibiki is one of the best sushi bars that I've ever visited in Kuala Lumpur. They serve the finest-quality, in-season ingredients imported from across the world, and strive to give patrons a true feel of the Japanese sushi-bar culture.All the fish served is fresh and "clean-tasting" (you can really taste all the flavours of the fish!), and the ratio of fish to rice is perfect (if you fill up easily, you can request for the chef to make your sushi with less rice). If you are lucky enough to catch the seasonal produce, I would highly recommend having a go at the saltwater uni, shinko fish, fresh ikura and fresh edamame. To keep up the practice of serving only the freshest ingredients, Sushi Hibiki operates with a set menu, but you are welcome to order any additional sushi / item that you fancy (with additional charges of course).Amazing food aside, Chef Sam and his team are very friendly thus creating a comfortable ambience in the restaurant. I've had some of the most beautiful dining experiences eating here with Sam and his team.The restaurant is quite small and exclusive, therefore prior reservations are recommended. I suggest taking a seat at the counter where you can watch the chefs at work, and engage in friendly conversation.

Author: Alfredo L.
Review: Truly 5 stars. I’ve eaten at many, many Michelin starred restaurants and honestly Lai Po Heen is worthy of one. Heck, this would be considered fantastic even by mainland Chinese standards. …MoreTruly 5 stars. I’ve eaten at many, many Michelin starred restaurants and honestly Lai Po Heen is worthy of one. Heck, this would be considered fantastic even by mainland Chinese standards.The food: I had a tasting menu featuring items like lobster in coconut sauce, braised duck leg, abalone soup, and a durian dessert platter.Each course was prepared immaculately. Crab was clearly fresh and seasoned well. The lobster was succulent and juicy while being well seasoned. The shell cracked perfectly so the meat would fall right out. The duck leg you could cut with a spoon and seasoned perfectly. The abalone soup was perfectly delicate with just the right amount of salinity. The durian desserts showcased the pungent flavor of durian without letting it overpower you.Service was also spectacular. My tea cup was never empty, finished courses were promptly ferried away, and fresh silverware was provided for the dishes that most required it. I felt I was being well attended to without being overwhelmed.Yes, it’s expensive. No, it’s not meant to be perfectly authentic— local flavors are definitely showcased here and fused with traditional Chinese classics. But it’s absolutely worth it. Whoever manages Lai Po Heen deserves a pat on the back— this is a world class dining experience.My only (minor) complaint would be that I wish the dress code was a bit more enforced. Not to the point of jacket and tie but I did see people there with Hawaiian shirts, flip flops, and cargo shorts. Kinda kills the vibe a bit.
Location: Kuala Lumpur City Centre, Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur

Author: M Lee
Review: The Grand Dame of Bukit Damansara, its been on my list for years and finally got around this place. Positioning itself as a fine dining Ceylonese cuisine. Most dishes centers around the main ingredient which is coconut, the spices used are …MoreThe Grand Dame of Bukit Damansara, its been on my list for years and finally got around this place. Positioning itself as a fine dining Ceylonese cuisine. Most dishes centers around the main ingredient which is coconut, the spices used are mild and not as aggressive as the neighbourly Indian cuisine.I've ordered some individual dishes to try out from fried, stew, and banana wrap dishes. Overall it is nice, the quality of the proteins can be improved and sourced differently, the tiger prawn for example at RM76.00 before tax per piece needs to have the 'wow' factor, the Sabah ones don't cut it, looks big but texture is like rubber after cooking.The alcohol beverages were ok, there was a bug in my house wine but only noticed it till the end. They do have Sri Lankan brewery beers which are interesting, I quite like the stout, it taste like alcoholic coffee.The service is thunder quick, very attentive and friendly staff's.

Author: Hafiznizam Hashim
Review: Evaluation of nasi kandar joints is highly subjective. There is no universal standard that can be applied, and in most cases, a verdict is formed based on personal biases. Any person ever to have stood patiently in a queue for a plate of …MoreEvaluation of nasi kandar joints is highly subjective. There is no universal standard that can be applied, and in most cases, a verdict is formed based on personal biases. Any person ever to have stood patiently in a queue for a plate of nasi kandar will lay claim that he is a nasi kandar connoisieur but nothing could be further from the truth. It is based on this premise that I dare say Nasi Kandar Yaseem is one of the better tasting nasi kandar in KL. This is arguable of course, that much is a given, and I will not hold that against anyone who would disagree with me. This is definitely not a "Fight Me" shout out. To me my nasi kandar, and to you, yours.Try the Ayam Masak Hitam, and let the expert behind the counter works his magic with the kuah campur. Indulgence can be in the form of a mid-size sotong kari. Go for the prawns if you feel like a million dollars. Get the half-cut salted egg too. Then sit and enjoy the glorious food.The restaurant is big enough to accomodate big party so there is no worry if you bring your whole family including your neighbours. And there is one section that is air-conditioned. You can also enjoy your nasi kandar by the road side, but I believe they only do this at night.This is definitely a fare worth coming back to.

Review: Had some fantastic food here. The nachos were alright but needed more chips; they gave a lot of salsa which was good but not a ton of chips. The loaded fries were okay but would have been better with the toppings mixed together instead of …MoreHad some fantastic food here. The nachos were alright but needed more chips; they gave a lot of salsa which was good but not a ton of chips. The loaded fries were okay but would have been better with the toppings mixed together instead of separate. The fries were fantastic though. The empanadas were okay overall; the breading outside was excellent but the filling wasn't exactly my favorite. The chorizo tapa was very yummy and mixed well with the loaded fries so I would recommend getting these two together. The arepitas were pretty good but not quite traditional. The fajitas were really tasty.The dessert here stole the show. We had the apple pie tacos which was a perfect blending of Mexican food with an apple pie type of dessert and it was really enjoyable. There was hot apple pie filling inside of tiny crunchy, sugary shells. There was some whipped cream as well which helped make them very light and balanced. Then there was a single scoop of ice cream which was a nice complement to the apple pie, but I found myself just eating most of it after finishing the tacos. This dish was more simple than if some truly amazing chef made it but it was very enjoyable. I would probably not share these with somebody since there are only 3 very small tacos and you'll end up fighting the other person for the third taco!

Review: its hard to find decent breakfast anywhere, but this place is open early. i was hesitant to eat here at first because i am a bit intimidated to eat at large restaurants and i was unsure about the tipping customs in malaysia. i walked around …Moreits hard to find decent breakfast anywhere, but this place is open early. i was hesitant to eat here at first because i am a bit intimidated to eat at large restaurants and i was unsure about the tipping customs in malaysia. i walked around a bit to see my options and looked at the mcdonalds menu and made my way back here and sat down. i had the roti made with egg and onion, then ordered the butter roti. i enjoyed both but prefer the egg and onion because the buttered is a bit too sweet for me. they have an efficient way for people to pay for food by using an rfid card that tracks what you ordered. you just bring it to the cashier and he gives you the total. my total came out to 9.85 ringgit, which i thought i was undercharged for because i had ordered the  second roti later, but it was all there. 4 myr for egg/onion roti, 3 myr for butter roti, and 2.30 for the tea tarik. there is a 6% service tax of 0.56 myr which got rounded down to 0.55 myr. cant get a cheaper breakfast than that at mcdonalds. the hostel that i am staying at is next to this restaurant. if there were more suitable hostels in the area i would probably stay near the central market area because i can see myself eating the same few things around here for an extended period. all travelers should try breakfast here at least once for the simple stuff like roti and tea. maybe observe some of what the locals are eating and be more adventurous with your order
